SRP Energy & Utility News

Stay informed about SRP rate changes, battery incentives, solar export credits, and programs that may impact Valley homeowners.

⚡ SRP Residential Prices Have Increased Year After Year

SRP's own published pricing history shows cumulative residential price changes rising from about 3% in 2021 to approximately 24% by 2025. That means residential customers have experienced a substantial increase in utility pricing over this period, reinforcing the value of reducing long-term exposure to future utility price changes. Actual bill impacts vary by usage and price plan.

⚠️ Get Off Peak Demand Usage

On SRP’s E-27 Customer Generation Plan, the goal is to avoid pulling large amounts of power from the grid during on-peak hours. SRP uses your single highest 30-minute average demand during the billing cycle to determine the monthly demand charge, so one big spike can cost hundreds. Solar and battery storage can help reduce that peak grid demand.

Example: 15 kW peak demand
May, June, September & October:
First 3 kW × $9.77 + next 7 kW × $16.24 + final 5 kW × $29.18 = $288.89 demand charge

July & August:
First 3 kW × $11.90 + next 7 kW × $19.97 + final 5 kW × $36.05 = $355.74 demand charge

That demand charge is separate from energy (kWh) charges and the monthly service charge. Rates shown are current published E-27 rates and may change.

🔋 SRP Will Pay Homeowners For Battery Support

SRP Battery Partner™ is SRP's virtual power plant-style battery program. Participating systems can earn up to $110 per average kW per year for helping support the grid during conservation events, based on performance.
